body: Accord, LLC acquired a parcel in the Hamlet of Accord, Town of Rochester, Ulster County, that is the site of a historic granary and seed mill complex, and asked the Town Board to rezone it into an Economic Enterprise Overlay (EEO) district and approve its conceptual development plan. After a SEQRA review ended in a negative declaration, the Town Board adopted Local Law No. 10 of 2023, granting the rezoning and approving a plan to convert the buildings into a restaurant, a bike shop, an artist gallery, a coworking space, worker housing and an inn. It agreed the project needed 63 parking spaces: 57 on site, 25 of them for the restaurant, and six off site.

During site plan review, Accord's architect told the Planning Board in May 2024 that the artist gallery would be dropped, the coworking space reduced by 421 square feet and the six off-site spaces eliminated. On July 8, 2024, the Planning Board granted conditional site plan approval, finding the modified project in substantial conformance with the conceptual plan and adopting the Town Board's on-site parking finding. In August 2024, two individuals with property near the site filed an Article 78 petition, arguing among other things that the restaurant needed 78 spaces under the code's one-space-per-50-square-feet standard applied to its listed 3,914.65 square feet. Accord's engineer responded that he had used an alternative one-space-per-three-seats calculation, presented to the Town Board, because the code does not say whether gross or net floor area applies. Supreme Court, Ulster County (Justice David Gandin) dismissed the petition in a judgment entered April 11, 2025.

Writing for a unanimous panel, Justice Christine M. Clark held the approval was not arbitrary or capricious. The EEO rules allow approval of a site plan in "substantial conformance" with the conceptual plan, and the changes here reduced the project's scope without adding a new use or changing on-site parking. The petitioners never asked the Planning Board to seek a code interpretation from the zoning board or code enforcement officer, and in any event the Planning Board did not interpret the code: the Town Board had accepted Accord's parking calculation in Local Law 10, and in EEO districts the code's parking standards are guidelines rather than strict requirements. The court also upheld dropping the six off-site spaces, which tracked the removal of the gallery and the smaller coworking space, and rejected an argument about an "unconditioned event space" because the Planning Board expressly declined to approve events as a use.

timeline.label: Town Board adopts Local Law No. 10 of 2023, rezoning the site and approving Accord's conceptual plan
Planning Board grants conditional site plan approval for the scaled-back project
Two neighboring property owners file an Article 78 petition
Supreme Court, Ulster County dismisses the petition
Third Department affirms, upholding the site plan approval
